outcomes: The Go and TypeScript extractors produce the same schema hash and the same JSON Schema for the same configuration.
A value marked sensitive never travels through the plaintext config store or inside an authored member.
A malformed manifest, entry, request or member is refused with a diagnostic before the server stores it.
nonGoals: Typed configuration loading, defaults and remote resolution at runtime, which the Go and TypeScript framework packages own.
A ProtocolVersion constant: the schema hash plays the role of a version.
Enforcing the advisory constraints a field declares.
The config server itself and its storage.

requirements.text: Each valid schema manifest, registered schema, config entry, secret entry, delete request and resolve-secrets request fixture parses and validates, and each invalid one is refused: a bad field type, hash prefix or map key, a misplaced composite slot, a missing appName, no configs, an unknown member, an entry with no values or a bad name, a delete with no path, and a secret envelope that is missing or not base64. Validation gives the same diagnostics on every run.

A publish-time manifest refuses an unknown member and the server-owned registeredAt, which only a registered manifest carries. Validation refuses a missing appName, empty configs, a hash without the sha256: prefix, a field type outside the vocabulary, a duplicate block path and a path with a slash, and accepts a scoped npm or Go module appName. A resolve request needs appName and environment.

The field types are string, int, float, bool, duration, object, array and map, and a map key is string, int or bool. schemas/schema-manifest.json lists exactly these, requires items on an array and keys and values on a map, and forbids those slots on any other type. @putnami/application's vocabulary matches the schema enums.

The Go extractor and @putnami/application's extractor map a sensitive field to sensitive: true, a production-unsafe default to productionUnsafeDefault, a nested struct to object fields, a list to array items and a map to keys and values. The Go framework's describe mode maps sensitive, nested, array and map fields the same way. All three refuse a non-primitive map key at build time.

The schema hash is sha256: and the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the canonical blocks, with paths and fields sorted recursively, so extraction order does not change it. An unset productionUnsafeDefault adds no byte and a set one changes the hash. The anchor sha256:884119c1a3fd2c7b and the hashes in the nested-hash and production-unsafe fixtures hold in Go and in @putnami/application, which also matches the typed-defaults one.

A manifest renders to the JSON Schema of the nested-hash and typed-defaults goldens in fixtures/jsonschema: each default is the JSON scalar of its declared type, an empty string default is omitted, a production-unsafe default renders x-production-unsafe-default: true, only opt-in fields are required, and an int or bool map key is a constrained string. @putnami/application renders the same goldens.

Resolution reads five layers with priorities 10 to 50, later winning by deep merge: */*, */env, app/*, app/env and, when a version is given, app/env/version. Without a version there are four. A deep merge overrides a nested key, keeps its siblings and adds new keys.

environment, path and version accept [a-zA-Z0-9.*_-]+. appName also accepts @ and / but refuses an empty, . or .. segment, so app/../etc and /etc/passwd fail. A name is at most 256 characters and only version may be empty. A values map holds at most 1000 keys. A sealed envelope needs keyUri, wrappedDek, nonce and ciphertext, and refuses one that is not base64.
AllScopes is exactly config.schema.read, config.schema.write, config.value.read, config.value.write, config.secret.read and config.secret.write.

A sensitive field written through the config store is an error, sensitive-in-config. A secret write whose fields are all non-sensitive is a warning, non-sensitive-in-secret. A write to a path absent from the registered schema is an error, matched on the longest dotted block. A recognized block also refuses an unknown field, a value of the wrong type and an invalid map key, and an unknown block is left to the path check.

An authored member is config.authored-member.v1 compact JSON with sorted fields, layers and references, so equivalent input gives the same bytes and descriptor, and its selection fingerprint moves with a value, pin, reference or required flag. A sensitive field carries an exact config-secret:// reference, never a value. A missing required value, a placeholder, an undeclared or overlapping path, a sensitive descendant, and bytes or digests that differ from the rebuild are refused.
